note: Independently re-judged 2026-10-28 after the ba03d7c2c7 ESP cipher change, from rfc/full/rfc4303.txt Section 3.2: "Note that although both confidentiality and integrity are optional, at least one of these services MUST be selected, hence both algorithms MUST NOT be simultaneously NULL." Read every tagged cover: TestIntegrityOnlyESPRefusals and both tags in TestIPsecESPRequiresIntegrity. The IKE test supplies an otherwise complete matching NULL/NONE proposal and requires the specific ErrProposalIncomplete, not an arbitrary refusal; espProposalComplete checks exactly that forbidden pair before matching. Its retained mutant disables that exact predicate rather than an unrelated parser error. The OSPF test's negative config has a valid ESP protocol and nonreserved SPI and requires ErrIPsecAuthAlgo for NULL/no integrity; its separate positive config adds valid SHA256 and a 32-octet key and requires successful validation. Thus its two tags name distinct inputs and assertions, not one assertion counted twice. validateIPsecInterface rejects absent/unknown integrity before any SA install. The changed parseESPProposal still requires a hash for every non-AEAD cipher, including NULL, and validates an explicitly provided hash through HashImplementedESP; the change admits ESP-only SHA1, not absent integrity. Read matchOfferedESP/espProposalMatches as well: non-AEAD responder selection resolves a configured integrity algorithm and requires it in the peer offer. Both halves of the sentence express the same exclusion; confidentiality-only support is optional, not an additional acceptance obligation. Retain enforced for the exact prohibition. Evidence boundary retained from the earlier judgment: the tagged IKE assertion exercises initiator answer validation, not the config parser or responder refusal directly; those latter guards were read, not newly execution-proven here. No test run or fresh red/green observation is claimed by this audit.
